title: Why a water main stays deferred

blocks.text: A water utility's capital plan chooses which mains to work on. Some mains have two options, reline or replace, in an alternative group: at most one option per main. For every project the plan defers, the utility's analyst has already forced it in and re-solved, so for each one there is the best plan and the forced plan. The asset managers want the reason written from those two plans, in the terms they use: which alternative the deferred option would push out, and which other projects would give way.

items: `group_of` maps a project to its alternative group; a project with no group is absent;
`best` is the set of projects in the best plan, and `forced` the set with `name` forced in, or `None` when no plan allows it.
`["infeasible"]` when there is no forced plan;
`["nothing displaced"]` when the forced plan drops nothing from the best one;

otherwise one entry per project the forced plan drops: `"alternative <id>"` when it is in the same alternative group as `name`, `"displaced <id>"` when it is not. Alternatives come first, then the rest, each part sorted by id.

blocks.text: The forced plan was solved with $`\sum_{t} x_{\text{name},t} = 1`$ added, and each group $`g`$ keeps $`\sum_{i \in g} \text{started}(i) \le 1`$. Before coding, say which of those rows makes a dropped project an "alternative", and what a project with no group can never have. The tests use their own mains.

from __future__ import annotations


def why_deferred(name: str, group_of: dict[str, str], best: set[str], forced: set[str] | None) -> list[str]:
    """Reasons a main left out of the best plan stays out, from the plan forced to include it.

    `group_of` maps a main to its alternative group (mains without one are absent). `forced` is the
    best plan with `name` forced in, or None when no plan allows it.
    """
    if forced is None:
        return ["infeasible"]
    dropped = sorted(best - forced - {name})
    if not dropped:
        return ["nothing displaced"]
    group = group_of.get(name)
    alternatives = [f"alternative {m}" for m in dropped if group is not None and group_of.get(m) == group]
    displaced = [f"displaced {m}" for m in dropped if group is None or group_of.get(m) != group]
    return alternatives + displaced


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(why_deferred("reline_M4", {"reline_M4": "M4", "replace_M4": "M4"}, {"replace_M4", "valve_V2"},
                       {"reline_M4"}))

cases.says: a deferred option names the alternative it would push out and the other projects that give way
a forcing with no feasible plan is reported as infeasible, not as giving nothing way
a forcing that drops nothing from the best plan says so
a project with no alternative group has no alternatives, even when ungrouped projects give way
alternatives are listed first, then the other projects, each sorted
